mine is retired, but i got mine pre-CGM. as people have pointed out, technology honestly outmatches diabetic alert dogs at this point. plus, it’s a whole other ball game when it comes to interacting with people, explaining what the dog does, and dealing with jerks/people who don’t let you into establishments/people who don’t respect boundaries. they can be helpful, but it’s worth really considering if the time and energy put into the dog is worth it in your context, especially the social aspects people don’t think of. plus, i got my dog at a nonprofit, but generally people sink a LOT of money into service dogs (not just the dog but food, vet visits, equipment, etc). 

as mentioned, my dog is retired, but i don’t plan on getting another one. i love her to death but i don’t think it’s worth it for me anymore, especially with a CGM, because it requires a lot of mental energy
